_note: The United Kingdom has no registration tax. What looks like one is the first year's VED licence, and a genuinely used import does not pay it at all — VERA 1994 s.62(1C) removes the first vehicle licence when the car was registered abroad more than 6 months ago AND has covered more than 6 000 km. Both limbs must be met. Everything here is in pounds and converted at the day's rate.

ved._note: Rates for licences taken out on or after 1 April 2026 (VERA 1994 Sch. 1, substituted by Finance Act 2026 s.92). The diesel column is for cars that do not meet Euro 6d — Euro 6d-TEMP does not count. The alternative-fuel discount was abolished on 1 April 2025, so petrol, hybrid and electric share the first column; a zero-emission car pays £10, not nothing.

supplement._note: Annual, not one-off, so it is named and not counted. It does reach imports: para. 1GE(1)(b) measures the six years from first registration anywhere, and the threshold is tested against a UK list price, not the invoice.

fees._note: One-off amounts actually collected at registration. Plates carry no official price — DVLA only requires a registered supplier — so that one is a market range, like every other estimate here.
